text.en: A full granary does not feed a hungry family if they cannot afford the grain or cannot digest it safely. Food security has three parts: availability, access and absorption.

Food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical, social and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food (FAO, 2009).
Dr M.S. Swaminathan said nutrition security means access to a balanced diet, safe drinking water, environmental hygiene, primary health care and primary education.
Availability is the physical presence of food stocks, depending on domestic production, changes in stocks and imports.
Access is mainly purchasing power, linked to employment, assets and education.
Absorption is the ability to biologically utilise the food eaten, which needs health and hygiene.
Food grain production rose with HYV seeds of rice and wheat: from about 54 million tonnes in the early 1950s on a little over 98 million hectares, with an average yield of 547 kg per hectare.
So food security depends both on the quantity of food and on people's ability to buy it and stay healthy.

problem.en: A country has record grain stocks but many poor families go hungry. Which component of food security is failing?

text.en: Availability is fine because stocks are high.
Access fails because the poor lack money to buy grain.
So production alone cannot ensure food security.

prompt.en: Explain the three components of food and nutrition security.

commonMisconceptions.en: Equating food security only with production

points.en: Access depends on income and employment.
HYV seeds raised grain production after the 1950s.
Nutrition security also needs water, hygiene and health care.
